name: Ecuador
description: Ecuador offers expats an appealing blend of a significantly lower cost of living and a high quality of life, set amidst diverse landscapes ranging from Andean mountains to Pacific coastlines. The country is known for its welcoming culture and a dollarized economy, which simplifies financial transitions for many expatriates.
longdescription: Expat life in Ecuador is characterized by its affordability and rich cultural experiences. Many expats, particularly retirees, find that their pensions and savings stretch considerably further here, allowing for a comfortable lifestyle. Major expat hubs like Cuenca, Quito, and coastal towns such as Manta offer established communities, modern amenities, and access to quality, affordable healthcare. The culture is a vibrant mix of indigenous, Spanish, and African influences, with Ecuadorians generally known for their warmth and hospitality, making integration easier for newcomers. Learning Spanish is highly recommended to build deeper connections with locals. The economy is dollarized, eliminating currency exchange rate concerns. While the political and security situation has seen volatility, particularly concerning drug cartels, targeted expat areas often maintain a sense of normalcy, emphasizing the importance of choosing locations wisely and practicing common-sense safety measures. The country's diverse geography provides various climates, from temperate 'eternal spring' in the mountains to tropical along the coast, catering to different preferences.

visas.name: Ecuador Retirement Visa
visas.description: Ecuador's retirement (Jubilado) visa requires just $800/month in pension income — one of the world's lowest thresholds. Uses US dollars, making budgeting straightforward.
benefits: Very low income requirement
USD economy — no currency risk
Galápagos access
Excellent climate in Cuenca
Import one vehicle duty-free
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 3 years as a temporary resident, eligible for permanent residency.
required_documents: Passport
Proof of pension income ($800+/month)
Criminal background check (apostilled)
Medical certificate
Passport photos

visas.name: Ecuador Digital Nomad Visa
visas.description: Temporary residency for remote workers with foreign-sourced income. Ecuador uses the US dollar, making financial planning easy for North American and European nomads.
benefits: Legal residency for 2 years
USD economy
Affordable cost of living
Four distinct ecosystems to explore
Path to permanent residency
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 3 years, eligible for permanent residency.
required_documents: Passport
Proof of remote income ($1,350+/month)
Health insurance
Criminal background check (apostilled)
Bank statements

visas.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Jubilado (Pensioner Visa)
visas.description: This visa grants temporary residency in Ecuador for foreign retirees whose primary source of income is a pension from public or private institutions located abroad. It allows the holder to live in Ecuador and access various resident benefits, with a clear pathway to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are retirees or individuals receiving a consistent, verifiable pension from a foreign source, seeking to establish residency in Ecuador.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 21 months of continuous temporary residency under this visa, applicants become eligible to apply for permanent residency in Ecuador.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa is renewable once for an additional two years. Must maintain health insurance and not be absent from Ecuador for more than 90 days in a calendar year during the temporary residency period to maintain eligibility for permanent residency.
visas.tax_implications: Standard resident tax rules apply; no specific tax exemptions or special treatments are mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Allows legal work and entrepreneurship in Ecuador.
Ability to include spouse and minor children as dependents.
Eligibility to obtain an Ecuadorian national ID card (Cédula).
Access to the Ecuadorian social security system (IESS) and discounts for seniors (65+).
Provides a direct path to permanent residency after 21 months of temporary residency.
required_documents: Color photograph (JPG, max 1MB, 5x5 cm, white background, neutral/natural smile, both eyes open).
Valid passport with a minimum validity of six months.
Original certificate of criminal records from the country of origin or countries of residence for the last five years, translated, apostilled or legalized (valid for 180 days from issuance).
Official document certifying monthly pension income from abroad (equal to or greater than three Unified Basic Salaries).
Bank statements showing consistent deposits of the pension income.
Proof of lawful means of living.
Health insurance (national or foreign) valid for the visa period.
Certified Spanish translations of apostilled documents.
Movimiento Migratorio (record of movements in and out of Ecuador).
Marriage certificate with apostille (if including spouse).
Birth certificates with apostilles (for any dependents).
application_process_steps: Gather and apostille/legalize required documents, including criminal background checks, pension verification letters, and any marriage/birth certificates. Ensure certified Spanish translations are obtained for apostilled documents.
Enter Ecuador legally, typically on a tourist visa (application can be submitted from within Ecuador or through an Ecuadorian consulate abroad).
Submit the visa application online via the Cancillería's e-visa portal, uploading all supporting documents, completing biometrics, and paying the application fee.
Await processing and approval of the visa application by the migration authorities.
Pay the visa granting fee upon approval.
Visit a Registro Civil office in Ecuador to obtain the national identity card (Cédula) after the visa is granted.

visas.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Rentista por Trabajo Remoto (Digital Nomad Visa)
visas.description: The 'Visa de Residencia Temporal de Rentista por Trabajo Remoto' (Digital Nomad Visa) in Ecuador is a temporary residence permit for foreign nationals who perform professional or service activities remotely for companies or clients domiciled outside of Ecuador. It allows beneficiaries to live in Ecuador while continuing to work for their foreign employer or business.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are remote workers, freelancers, or business owners whose income is generated from sources outside of Ecuador.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 21 months of continuous temporary residency under this visa, applicants may qualify to apply for permanent residency in Ecuador. After three years of permanent residency, one can apply for Ecuadorian citizenship, and dual citizenship is recognized.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must continue to meet the income threshold and maintain compliance with immigration laws.
benefits: Legal right to reside in Ecuador for up to two years, renewable.
Ability to obtain an Ecuadorian identity card (Cédula).
Opportunity to open bank accounts in Ecuador.
Eligibility to affiliate with the Ecuadorian Social Security Institute (IESS).
Potential path to permanent residency and eventually citizenship.
required_documents: Color photograph (5x5 cm, white background, neutral or natural smile, both eyes open, JPG format, max 1 MB).
Valid passport with a minimum validity of six months.
Proof of remote work or business ownership outside Ecuador (e.g., apostilled employment contract or registered business documentation).
Bank statements reflecting monthly income from foreign sources for the three months prior to the application, or proof of 36 Unified Basic Salaries (SBU) per year.
Health insurance coverage valid for the duration of the visa.
Apostilled criminal background check from the country of origin or countries of residence for the last five years.
Additional documents as required by the mobility authority.
application_process_steps: Gather all necessary documents, ensuring apostilles and certified Spanish translations where required.
Submit the visa application virtually through the official e-VISAS platform of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility.
Pay the application fee ($50 USD for the application, $400 USD for the visa if accepted).
Attend a visa appointment at an Ecuadorian embassy, consulate, or zonal office (if required) to verify identity and documents.
Wait for the application to be processed and approved.
Physically submit documents to the embassy or consulate after visa issuance within one month to avoid cancellation.

visas.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Trabajo (Work Visa)
visas.description: The Visa de Residencia Temporal de Trabajo is an authorization granted by the Ecuadorian State to foreign individuals who intend to establish themselves in the country to carry out lawful work activities under an employment relationship. It permits temporary residence and legal work within Ecuador for a specific period.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is intended for foreign nationals who have been hired by a legally registered Ecuadorian company and will work in the country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of the temporary work visa can apply for permanent residency after completing 21 months of continuous temporary residency in Ecuador. During this period, applicants must not have been absent from Ecuador for more than 90 days per calendar year. After three years of permanent residency, individuals may be eligible to apply for Ecuadorian citizenship through naturalization.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa is renewable, subject to maintaining legal stay, compliance with Ecuadorian laws, and continued employment or demonstration of lawful means of livelihood.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of this visa will be subject to Ecuador's standard tax residency rules. If an individual resides in Ecuador for more than 183 days in a year, they become a tax resident and are generally taxed on their worldwide income, with potential exemptions for foreign income already taxed abroad.
benefits: Ability to legally work in Ecuador for a registered employer.
Grants temporary residency for up to two years.
Provides a clear pathway to permanent residency after 21 months.
Allows for dependents (spouse and children) to join the applicant in Ecuador.
Enables access to public services, including the Ecuadorian social security system (IESS), and allows opening bank accounts.
required_documents: Color photograph in JPG format (max 1 MB, 5x5 cm / 2x2 inches, updated, white background, neutral expression or natural smile, both eyes open).
Valid passport with a minimum validity of six (6) months.

Original criminal record certificate from the country of origin or countries of residence during the last five years, apostilled or legalized and officially translated into Spanish (valid for 180 days from issuance, required for applicants over 18 years old).
Proof of regular stay in the country from where the visa is being applied (if applying from outside Ecuador).
Proof of economic solvency or lawful means of livelihood, as per Ministerial Agreement No. 70 of June 28, 2024.
Completed visa application form.
Certificate of valid private health insurance.
Employment contract or letter of sponsorship/personnel action from a legally registered Ecuadorian company.
Curriculum Vitae of the applicant in Spanish.

Documents from the sponsoring company: Legal registration as a business, updated RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes), appointment of the legal representative (President, General Manager, or Attorney) registered in the Mercantile Registry, updated certificate of no pending obligations with IESS (Instituto Ecuatoriano de Seguridad Social), and company bylaws demonstrating capital increase if applicable.
application_process_steps: Register on the official e-VISAS virtual platform of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility.
Upload all required documents and the digital photograph to the online platform.
Pay the non-refundable application fee of USD $50.
The application will be reviewed by the immigration authorities.
Upon approval of the visa, pay the visa grant fee of USD $270.
If applying from abroad, travel to Ecuador. Once in Ecuador and with the visa granted, obtain the 'cédula' (Ecuadorian identification card) at the Civil Registry offices.

visas.name: Visa de Profesional, Técnico, Tecnólogo o Artesano
visas.description: The 'Visa de Profesional, Técnico, Tecnólogo o Artesano' is a temporary residency visa for foreign nationals who hold a professional, technical, technological degree, or artisan certification. It allows them to reside and work legally in Ecuador and provides a pathway to permanent residency.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals with accredited higher education degrees (Bachelor's, Master's, PhD, technical, or technological) or artisan qualifications who wish to live and work in Ecuador.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 21 months of temporary residency under this visa, applicants are eligible to apply for permanent residency. After 3 years as a permanent resident, applicants may apply for Ecuadorian citizenship through naturalization.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain lawful means of living and adhere to absence rules (not exceeding 90 days outside Ecuador per calendar year to maintain temporary residency status for permanent residency eligibility).
benefits: Ability to work legally in Ecuador in their field of expertise.
Opportunity to open a business in Ecuador.
Obtain an Ecuadorian national identification card (cédula).
Affiliate with the Ecuadorian Social Security Institute (IESS).
Open checking and savings accounts with Ecuadorian banks and cooperatives.
Ship household possessions duty-free to Ecuador.
Path to permanent residency and ultimately citizenship.
required_documents: Valid passport with at least 6 months remaining validity.
Passport-sized color photo with a white background, neutral expression, and both eyes open.
Criminal background certificate from country of origin or countries of residence for the last 5 years, apostilled or legalized and translated to Spanish (valid for 180 days from issuance).
Proof of current legal status in Ecuador (e.g., tourist entry stamp or valid visa), if applying from within Ecuador.
Professional, technical, or technologist degree, apostilled or legalized if issued abroad, and translated to Spanish.
Registration of the professional, technical, or technologist degree with SENESCYT (Ecuador's higher education authority) or artisan activity with the competent authority in Ecuador.
Proof of lawful means of living (e.g., bank statements, employment contracts) demonstrating at least 1x SBU income.
Visa application form.
application_process_steps: Gather and apostille/legalize all necessary documents in your home country (e.g., degree, criminal background check).
Enter Ecuador on a tourist visa (if applicable) and initiate the SENESCYT degree recognition process.
Complete the online visa application form and upload all required documents, paying the application fee.
Submit your application and await government review by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility.
Upon approval, pay the visa grant fee and receive your temporary professional visa.
Obtain your cédula (Ecuadorian national ID card) after visa approval and ensure continuous health insurance coverage.

visas.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Estudiante (Student Visa)
visas.description: The 'Visa de Residencia Temporal de Estudiante' is a temporary residency authorization granted by the Ecuadorian state to foreign nationals intending to establish themselves in the country for academic studies, including basic, secondary, undergraduate, postgraduate, language schools, or pre-professional/professional internships at officially recognized educational institutions.
visas.target_applicant: This visa is for foreign nationals who have been admitted to study at an educational institution officially recognized by the Ecuadorian government.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding the student visa for at least 21 months and maintaining continuous physical presence in Ecuador (no more than 90 days outside the country), applicants can apply for permanent residency. After three years of permanent residency, it's possible to apply for Ecuadorian citizenship through naturalization.
visas.renewal_conditions: Renewal requires presenting updated requirements related to the continuation of studies or pre-professional/professional practices.
benefits: Legal residency in Ecuador for the duration of the academic program, up to two years.
Renewable for the continuation of studies or professional practices.
Provides a direct path to permanent residency after 21 months of continuous presence in Ecuador.
required_documents: Valid passport with a minimum of six months remaining validity, plus a photocopy.
Passport-size color photograph (JPG format, maximum 1 MB, 5x5 cm / 2x2 inches, white background, neutral expression or natural smile with both eyes open).
Enrollment or admission certificate from an accredited Ecuadorian educational institution, confirming full name, program of study, and duration of the academic period.

Certificate of clean criminal record from the country of origin or the country of residence for the last five years, apostilled or legalized and translated if necessary, valid for up to 180 days from its issuance.
Proof of lawful financial means (Solvencia Económica) to cover living expenses, generally showing at least $500 USD per month and a $1,000 USD deposit.
Proof of health insurance that covers the stay in Ecuador.
Completed visa application form.
For minors: Special power of attorney or authorization from absent parent(s), apostilled or legalized and translated if applicable, and apostilled/legalized birth certificate.
application_process_steps: Secure an enrollment or admission letter from an officially recognized Ecuadorian educational institution.
Gather all required documents, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and translated into Spanish as needed.
Create an account on Ecuador's virtual consulate system (e-visa portal) via cancilleria.gob.ec.
Submit the application online, upload all required documents, and pay the non-refundable $50 USD application fee.
Schedule and attend an appointment at the nearest Ecuadorian consulate (if applying from abroad) or Zonal Coordination office (if applying within Ecuador).
Pay the visa issuance fee of $100 USD upon approval of the visa.

visas.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Inversionista (Investor Visa)
visas.description: This visa grants temporary residency to foreign individuals who make a qualified investment in Ecuador in real estate, a certificate of deposit, or shares in an Ecuadorian company. It allows the holder to reside, work, and conduct business activities in the country.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals looking to invest capital in Ecuador, typically through real estate purchases, bank deposits, or business investments, with the intention of establishing residency.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After holding the temporary investor visa for 21 months, and maintaining the qualifying investment, the visa holder is eligible to apply for permanent residency in Ecuador. Time spent on a dependent visa also counts towards permanent residency eligibility.
visas.renewal_conditions: The investment must be maintained. To renew, the applicant must present a valid passport, migratory movement certificate, and updated proof of the investment. For permanent residency, the holder cannot be outside Ecuador for more than 90 days in total during the 21 months of temporary residency.
visas.tax_implications: Standard resident tax rules apply to income and investments in Ecuador, including taxes on capital gains. It is advisable to consult with a tax professional regarding specific tax obligations related to investments and residency.
benefits: Ability to legally work in Ecuador.
Can sponsor dependants (spouse and children).
Permits opening a business in the country.
Eligibility to obtain an Ecuadorian national ID (cédula).
Allows affiliation with the Ecuadorian Social Security Institute (IESS).
Opportunity to ship household possessions duty-free to Ecuador.
Path to permanent residency and eventually citizenship.
required_documents: Color photograph (JPG, max 1MB, 5x5 cm or 2x2 inches, white background, neutral or natural smile, both eyes open).
Valid passport with a minimum validity of six (6) months.

Original criminal record certificate from the country of origin or countries of residence for the last five years, apostilled or legalized, and translated into Spanish (valid for 180 days from emission).

Proof of a qualifying investment in Ecuador (e.g., property deed for real estate, certificate of deposit from an Ecuadorian financial institution for a minimum of 2 years, or proof of investment in company shares).
Evidence of lawful means of living for the applicant and dependants.
Apostilled birth certificate for children (if applicable).
Apostilled marriage certificate for spouse (if applicable).
Proof of family relationship (for dependants).
Documents in a foreign language must be translated into Spanish and authenticated (apostilled or legalized).
application_process_steps: Make the qualifying investment in Ecuador (real estate, CD, or business shares).
Gather all required documents, ensuring they are apostilled/legalized and translated into Spanish where necessary.
Submit the visa application online through the official platform of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility.
Pay the application fee and the visa authorization fee.
Await approval and instructions from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility.
Once the visa is granted, obtain the Ecuadorian national ID (cédula), presenting proof of health insurance at this stage.

visas.name: Visa de Amparo (Family Sponsorship/Family Reunification Visa)
visas.description: The Visa de Amparo, or Family Sponsorship/Family Reunification Visa, allows close family members of an Ecuadorian citizen or a foreign resident (holding either a temporary or permanent visa) to legally reside in Ecuador. It is granted based on maintaining family ties and facilitates family reunification within the country.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are spouses, common-law partners, and minor children (under 18) of an Ecuadorian citizen or a foreign temporary/permanent resident; parents can be sponsored once the principal obtains permanent residency.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The temporary Visa de Amparo can lead to permanent residency. After 21 continuous months of temporary residency, both the principal and their dependents can apply for permanent residency, provided they meet specific conditions, including limited time outside Ecuador and continued financial solvency. Holders of the permanent 'Visa de Amparo' may apply for citizenship after 2 years.
visas.renewal_conditions: For temporary Amparo visas, renewal depends on the validity and renewal of the principal (amparante)'s visa, and maintaining the family ties. For transition to permanent residency, applicants must not be outside Ecuador for more than 90 days total during the 21-month temporary residency period, demonstrate continued financial means, and have a current criminal background check.
visas.tax_implications: Standard resident tax rules apply; no specific tax exemptions or special treatments are mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Ability to live in Ecuador indefinitely (for permanent visa) or for the duration of the amparante's visa (for temporary visa).
Freedom to work in any job or business in Ecuador (especially for permanent visa holders).
Eligibility to apply for Ecuadorian citizenship after two years of permanent residency.
Access to the public healthcare system (IESS).
Unrestricted travel in and out of Ecuador.
required_documents: Updated color photograph (5x5 cm, JPG format up to 1MB, white background, neutral or natural smile, both eyes open).
Valid passport (original and copy) with a minimum validity of six months.

Original criminal record certificate from the country of origin or countries of residence for the last five years, apostilled or legalized, and translated to Spanish if necessary (required for applicants 18 years and older, valid for 180 days from issuance).
Documents proving the family relationship (e.g., marriage certificate, birth certificate, registered common-law partnership), apostilled or legalized and translated to Spanish if applicable.
Proof of lawful means of subsistence to support the sponsored individuals.
For minors, a special power of attorney or authorization (apostilled or legalized and translated) if one parent is absent.
Proof of regular stay in the country from which the application is made (if applying from abroad).
application_process_steps: Register on the official e-VISAS platform of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility.
Complete all required registration data on the platform.
Submit the online visa application form.
Pay the application fee (USD 50) and the visa authorization fee (USD 200 for temporary, potentially USD 270 for temporary dependent).
Upload or present all required supporting documents.

visas.name: Visa MERCOSUR
visas.description: The Visa MERCOSUR (Temporary Residence) is an authorization granted by the Ecuadorian state to foreign nationals from MERCOSUR member or associated states who intend to reside in Ecuador to engage in lawful activities. It allows for temporary residence and work in the country.
visas.target_applicant: Nationals of Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Paraguay, Peru, or Uruguay who wish to establish legal residency and work in Ecuador.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 21 months of continuous temporary residence on the Mercosur visa, applicants can apply for permanent residency. Absences from Ecuador must not exceed 90 cumulative days during this period. The Mercosur agreement also provides a direct path to permanent residency, allowing application before temporary visa expiration, provided the 21-month residency threshold is met and proof of IESS affiliation or tax returns is submitted.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa is renewable for an additional two years. Renewal is contingent on maintaining lawful means of subsistence and a clean criminal record.
benefits: Full work authorization in Ecuador.
Two-year initial validity, renewable for an additional two years.
Provides a direct path to permanent residency after 21 months of continuous temporary residence.
Government fees are lower compared to standard temporary residence visas.
required_documents: Color photograph (JPG, max 1MB, 5x5 cms/2x2 inches, updated, white background, neutral expression or natural smile, both eyes open).
Valid passport with a minimum of six months remaining validity.

Original criminal record certificate from the country of origin or where the applicant has resided for the last five years, translated, apostilled or legalized (valid for 180 days from issuance for applicants over 18 years old).
Proof of lawful means of subsistence (e.g., employment contracts, bank statements, business registration, IESS contribution certificates) as per Ministerial Agreement No. 70 of June 28, 2024.
application_process_steps: Enter Ecuador lawfully (Mercosur nationals can enter without a visa for up to 180 days to gather documents and begin the process).

Obtain original criminal background certificates from your country of origin or countries where you have resided for the past five years. These must be apostilled/legalized and translated into Spanish.
Prepare documentation proving lawful means of subsistence (e.g., employment contracts, bank statements, business registration, or IESS affiliation).

Create an account on the eVISA portal (serviciosdigitales.cancilleria.gob.ec) of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility and submit the application virtually, including all required documents and paying the non-refundable application fee of USD 50.
Await government review and approval. Upon approval, pay the visa grant fee of USD 200.
After visa approval, obtain health insurance (either private insurance or IESS affiliation) to secure the cédula (national identification card).

visas.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Rentista (Passive Income Visa)
visas.description: The 'Visa de Residencia Temporal de Rentista' is a temporary residency visa for foreign citizens who wish to reside in Ecuador based on a stable, passive income. This visa allows individuals to live in Ecuador without actively working in the local economy.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals with reliable and passive income from sources such as rentals, investments, dividends, annuities, trust distributions, royalties, or bond interest, who are not seeking employment in Ecuador.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 21 months of holding the temporary Rentista Visa, applicants become eligible to apply for permanent residency. Permanent residency does not have an ongoing income requirement.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must demonstrate that the passive income still meets the established threshold, usually with updated bank statements and source documentation.
benefits: Allows inclusion of family members (spouse and children) as dependents.
Provides a clear path to permanent residency after 21 months.
Initial validity of two years, with the possibility of renewal.
No maximum age requirement, suitable for all ages.
Does not require a significant investment or donation.
Permits dual or multiple citizenships.
required_documents: Valid passport with a minimum of six months validity remaining.
Criminal background check from the country of origin or any country of residence during the past five years.
Proof of passive income (e.g., rental contracts, investment titles, bank statements, pension benefits) certifying monthly lawful passive income.
Six months of bank statements showing regular deposits of the required income.
National or foreign health insurance valid for the full duration of the visa.
Color photograph (5x5 cm or 2x2 inches), updated, with a white background, neutral facial expression, or natural smile, with both eyes open.
Application form.
application_process_steps: Register on the official virtual consulate platform (consuladovirtual.gob.ec).
Choose the 'Residencia Temporal de Rentista' trámite and upload all required documents in PDF format.
Pay the visa application request fee (USD $50).
Wait for consular authorization to pay the visa granting fee (USD $400).
Schedule an interview date with the consulate or zonal office.
Receive the visa via email upon approval.

visas.name: Visa de Residencia Permanente por Tiempo de Permanencia Temporal
visas.description: This visa grants permanent residency to foreign nationals who have maintained temporary residency in Ecuador for at least 21 continuous months. It allows individuals to establish themselves indefinitely in the country, engage in lawful activities, and offers a pathway to Ecuadorian citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals who have already held a temporary resident visa in Ecuador for a minimum of 21 months and intend to establish permanent roots in the country.
visas.path_to_residency_description: This visa *is* permanent residency. It leads to potential Ecuadorian citizenship after meeting additional requirements.
visas.renewal_conditions: This visa is permanent; however, to maintain it, the holder cannot be absent from Ecuador for more than 180 days during each of the first two years. After the first two years, the holder can be absent for up to two years to retain the visa.
benefits: Ability to work legally in Ecuador
Right to open a business in Ecuador
Eligibility to obtain an Ecuadorian identity card (cédula) as a permanent resident
Option to affiliate with the Ecuadorian Institute of Social Security (IESS)
Can open current and savings accounts in Ecuadorian banks and cooperatives
Qualifies for Ecuadorian citizenship in the future, subject to meeting further requirements
required_documents: Color photograph (JPG format, max 1MB, 5x5 cm or 2x2 inches, updated, white background, neutral facial expression or natural smile, both eyes open)
Valid passport with a minimum validity of six months
Proof of lawful means of living, demonstrating a monthly income of at least the basic unified salary of Ecuador for the last three months (currently USD 460)
Ecuadorian criminal record certificate (for individuals over 18 years old)
Proof of continuous temporary residence in Ecuador for at least 21 months
Current temporary visa (must be valid before starting the process)
Birth certificate (for minors, apostilled or legalized and translated if applicable)
Special power of attorney or authorization (for minors, if one parent is absent, apostilled or legalized and translated if applicable)
application_process_steps: Review characteristics, requirements, and procedures on the official website of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility (MREMH).
Prepare all necessary documentation, ensuring all foreign documents are apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish.
Access the MREMH's eVisas portal or relevant online system to initiate the application.
Select 'Visa de Residencia Permanente por Tiempo de Permanencia' as the visa type.
Pay the application form fee ($50) and the visa fee ($225).
Submit the application and attend any required interviews at a Zonal Directorate in Ecuador or an Ecuadorian Consulate abroad.
If approved, present your passport for the visa endorsement and obtain the order for cedulation (Ecuadorian ID card), for which an additional $10 fee applies.

visas.name: Visa Humanitaria (Humanitarian Visa)
visas.description: The 'Visa Humanitaria' in Ecuador is primarily for individuals seeking international protection, such as asylum seekers, refugees, or stateless persons, whose applications for protection have been admitted. It also covers those with exceptional humanitarian reasons, including victims of natural disasters, environmental disasters, or human trafficking. This visa grants temporary residency and allows the holder to carry out any lawful activity within Ecuador.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are individuals whose request for international protection has been admitted by the competent authority, persons recognized as refugees, asylum seekers, or stateless, or those demonstrating exceptional humanitarian circumstances.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The humanitarian visa, particularly for those recognized under a protection status, is the main requirement to access the 'Visa de Protección Internacional.' This visa grants temporary residency for two years and can be renewed indefinitely, offering a clear path to longer-term residency in Ecuador.
visas.renewal_conditions: The visa may be renewed if the application for international protection has been admitted, or if the exceptional humanitarian reasons that led to its concession persist.
visas.tax_implications: Standard resident tax rules apply; there are no specific tax exemptions or special treatments mentioned for this visa category.
benefits: Grants temporary residency in Ecuador.
Allows the visa holder to undertake any lawful activity in Ecuador.
Provides a legal stay while an international protection request is being resolved.
Can be renewed until the underlying humanitarian or protection reasons cease.
Serves as a pathway to other migratory categories and potentially permanent residency.
required_documents: Passport (valid, or up to 5 years expired for Venezuelan citizens applying for VERHU).
Certificate of criminal record from country of origin or last 5 years of residence, apostilled or legalized by authorized entities.
Proof of a submitted and admitted application for international protection (for renewal of temporary visitor humanitarian visa).
Personal email address.
Official visa application forms, correctly completed.
Consular-type photographs.
For family group applications: birth certificates, marriage certificates, or other kinship documents, duly apostilled or legalized.
For minors: birth certificates, duly apostilled or legalized, and powers of attorney for travel if applicable.
application_process_steps: Access the official online platform (e.g., Consulado Virtual for VERHU, or the MREMH online services).
Register and create an account if required (for VERHU, this involves registering as a Venezuelan citizen).
Complete the visa application form with all requested personal and supporting information.
Pay the application form fee (currently $50 USD for VERHU; the visa itself may be free for specific humanitarian cases).
Attach all required documents electronically.
The relevant Zonal Directorate or consular office will communicate with the applicant to continue the process.

visas.name: Visa de Residencia Temporal de Religioso o Voluntario Religioso
visas.description: This visa grants temporary residency to foreign citizens who intend to reside in Ecuador to perform religious activities or religious volunteering. It is for individuals affiliated with an organization that has recognized legal status in Ecuador, and not directly linked to the Ecuadorian Episcopal Conference for this specific temporary visa.
visas.target_applicant: The ideal applicant is a foreign citizen who will perform religious activities or religious volunteering for a legally recognized religious organization in Ecuador.

### Visas & Notes
- Retirement visa: $800/month income requirement (one of lowest in world)
- Digital nomad visa: $1,350/month income required
- Investor visa: invest $30,000+ in Ecuador

Citizenship by Descent.desc: Ecuador recognizes *jus soli* and *jus sanguinis* without limitation. Individuals born outside Ecuador to at least one natural-born Ecuadorian parent are generally eligible for citizenship by descent, regardless of where they were born, their current age, or whether they have ever lived in Ecuador [18, 23, 27]. Eligibility typically requires the parent to have been born in Ecuador; if a parent naturalized, eligibility depends on specific circumstances at the time of the applicant's birth [23]. Dual citizenship is permitted, and there is no age cutoff for claiming this birthright [23, 27, 28]. Required documents usually include the applicant's original birth certificate (apostilled/legalized and translated), the parent's Ecuadorian identification (cédula, passport, or birth certificate), and proof of the parent-child relationship. Name discrepancies across documents are common but solvable [23, 27].

Naturalization.desc: Foreign nationals can apply for naturalization after a continuous and legal residence of at least three years in Ecuador [18, 28]. Applicants must be adults, provide a birth certificate, a copy of a valid passport, a criminal record certificate from their country of origin (and any country resided in for the last five years prior to arrival), and proof of sufficient economic means for subsistence [28]. An interview is required, where applicants must state their motives for becoming a citizen, ideally in Spanish, and demonstrate knowledge of the country [18]. Absences from Ecuador should not exceed 180 days per year during the first three years of permanent residency (this restriction may not apply for those qualifying via an Ecuadorian family member or spouse) [18]. Dual citizenship is recognized [28].

Birthright.desc: Persons born in Ecuador are considered Ecuadorian citizens by birth (*jus soli*) without exception [18, 21]. This means that children born on Ecuadorian soil automatically acquire Ecuadorian nationality.

Spouse and Family.desc: Permanent residents married to or in a permanent civil relationship with an Ecuadorian citizen may qualify for naturalization after two years of continuous residency in Ecuador [18]. The restriction on not being absent from Ecuador for more than 180 days per year during the initial residency period may not apply to those qualifying through marriage [18]. Eligibility for permanent residency also extends to those married to an Ecuadorian citizen or related by at least the second degree of consanguinity (e.g., sharing a grandparent) [18].

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax (PIT):** Tax residents are subject to progressive rates on their worldwide income, ranging from 0% to 37% in 2024. Non-tax residents pay a flat rate of 25% only on Ecuador-sourced income [5, 6]. The first $11,902 of income for tax residents is tax-free in 2024 [5].
*   **Temporary Tax Residency Regime (new as of 2024):** Qualifying non-residents who have not previously held Ecuadorian tax resident status may pay income tax only on Ecuador-sourced income for a period of five years. This offers significant advantages for those with foreign-sourced income like overseas pensions [6, 12].
*   **Value Added Tax (VAT):** The VAT rate was permanently increased to 13% as of April 1, 2024, and temporarily raised to 15% until December 31, 2024, by Presidential Decree [4, 11, 12]. Individuals 65 and older may request a refund, with a limit (e.g., $110 per month, which may rise) [4].
*   **Capital Outflow Tax (ISD):** This tax applies at a rate of 5% (as of April 1, 2024) to any movement of money out of Ecuador, whether electronic or physical. This includes wire transfers and settling foreign credit card balances from an Ecuadorian bank account [4, 6, 11, 12]. Dividends are exempt under certain considerations [11].
*   **Corporate Taxes:** Businesses pay taxes at rates of 22%, 25%, or 28%, depending on their structure and location. New businesses may qualify for reduced rates [5].
*   **Property Taxes:** Generally very low, with annual property taxes for a large house potentially being a few hundred dollars or less, and sometimes as low as $25 [2, 3, 17].
*   **Reporting Obligations:** Tax residents with income exceeding $11,902 in 2024 must file. Assets held abroad above $230,000 per person must be reported, though they are not currently taxed. Income from overseas employers for digital nomads currently has no established tax laws or reporting requirements in Ecuador [4, 5].
*   **Double Taxation Agreements:** Ecuador is a member of the Andean Community (Decision 578) to avoid double taxation among member states. It also has bilateral tax agreements with several other countries, including a formal agreement with the UK in 2024 [6].
*   **Interest on Savings:** Interest on savings accounts and CDs held for at least 183 days is not taxable [4].
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Ecuador offers a remarkably low cost of living. A comfortable budget for a single person can range from $1,000 to $1,500 per month, while a couple might live well on $1,500 to $2,500, including rent, utilities, food, and transportation [3, 7, 13, 19]. Rent for a one-bedroom apartment in a city can be $300-$600, and often includes furnishings [3, 7, 13, 20]. Groceries are inexpensive, especially at local markets [2, 3, 17].
*   **Language:** Spanish is the official language [2, 31]. While English speakers can be found, particularly in metropolitan areas and among doctors, learning Spanish is crucial for deeper integration and daily life [7, 20]. Google Translate can be helpful [20].
*   **Safety:** Ecuador's security situation has been volatile due to narcotrafficking, with a nationwide state of emergency declared in January 2024 [2, 15, 30]. However, safety varies significantly by region. Expats generally find Cuenca, Vilcabamba, and Cotacachi to be safe. Quito is generally safe with awareness, while Guayaquil carries higher risk [15, 32]. Common sense precautions like avoiding flashy displays of wealth, being mindful of surroundings, and using trusted transportation are essential [15, 32]. Protests and demonstrations can occur and may become violent, so avoid these areas and follow local authorities' instructions [30].
*   **Registration & Visas:** Ecuador has expat-friendly visa policies, including options for retirees, investors, entrepreneurs, professionals, and remote workers [3, 7, 19, 20, 31]. The retirement (Jubilado) visa currently requires proof of at least $1,410 per month in guaranteed income (three times the 2025 basic wage of $470) [19]. Most documents submitted to immigration authorities must be apostilled or legalized and translated into Spanish [31].
*   **Healthcare:** Both public and private healthcare services are available, with private care offering high quality at a fraction of North American costs. Residents are eligible to join the country's Social Security healthcare system, with premiums under $80 a month for a couple [2, 7]. Many doctors in metropolitan areas are foreign-trained and may speak English [7].
*   **Elderly Benefits:** Residents aged 65 and older receive special benefits, including half-price public transportation [2].
*   **Driving:** A car can be an optional expense in many areas due to good public transportation. Car registration costs approximately $166 annually [2, 17].
*   **Water & Food:** Tap water is generally not safe to drink in most places; boiling or buying water is recommended. Be careful when preparing food, ensuring fruits and vegetables are cleaned thoroughly [8].
*   **Bureaucracy:** Be prepared for slower processes and bureaucracy; patience is key [14, 20].
